questions.question: A Foundry agent calls a knowledge base through its MCP tool by using the project's managed identity. Every call returns 403. What should you do?

options.text: Increase the agent's retrieval reasoning effort to medium
options.why: Effort changes query planning, not authorization.

options.text: Assign the Search Index Data Reader role to the project's managed identity on the search service
options.why: Correct. Read-only access to the indexes is the least privilege the call needs.

options.text: Add a semantic configuration to the knowledge base
options.why: This does not grant access.

options.text: Assign the Owner role to the agent on the resource group
options.why: Owner is excessive, and agents are not role assignees.

questions.explanation: The identity that calls the search service needs a data-plane read role.

questions.question: Users ask two-part questions such as "Can I expense a taxi, and how long do I have to claim it?". You want the knowledge base to split them into subqueries. What should you configure?

options.text: A scoring profile on the index
options.why: Scoring profiles do not split questions.

options.text: A retrieval reasoning effort of minimal
options.why: Minimal skips model planning and sends the question as it is.

options.text: A retrieval reasoning effort of low or medium, with a chat model deployment for query planning
options.why: Correct. Model-based planning breaks the question into subqueries.

options.text: A larger chunk size in the Text Split skill
options.why: Chunk size is an indexing setting.

questions.explanation: Low and medium effort use a model to plan subqueries.

questions.question: An agent must say that it does not know when the knowledge base returns nothing relevant, and cite sources otherwise. Where should you put these requirements?

options.text: In the semantic configuration of the index
options.why: This names fields for ranking.

options.text: In the diagnostic settings of the search service
options.why: Diagnostics record telemetry. They do not control behaviour.

options.text: In the data source definition of the indexer
options.why: The data source defines where files are, not how answers are written.

options.text: In the agent's instructions, together with the knowledge base tool
options.why: Correct. Instructions govern how the agent uses retrieved content.

questions.explanation: Grounding behaviour is set in the agent instructions, supported by good retrieval.

questions.question: Several agents must share one curated source of company policies with planned subqueries and citations. Which design fits?

options.text: One knowledge base with knowledge sources, connected to each agent as a tool
options.why: Correct. A knowledge base can be shared by multiple agents.

options.text: Memory configured with a user profile
options.why: Memory stores facts learned about users, not curated documents.

options.text: A function tool that runs a SQL query for each question
options.why: This does not provide planned retrieval or citations.

options.text: A separate file search vector store uploaded to every agent
options.why: File search suits per-agent or per-conversation files, and it duplicates the content.

questions.explanation: Knowledge bases are the shared grounding layer for agents.

questions.question: Which two statements about connecting a workflow or application to a knowledge base are correct?

options.text: A knowledge base can be used only by agents created in the Foundry portal
options.why: Applications and other frameworks can call it too.

options.text: An application can call the knowledge base retrieve API or an SDK, without using an agent
options.why: Correct. Any client that can call the REST API can use it.

options.text: Retrieval always requires a chat model, even at minimal effort
options.why: Minimal effort extraction from an index does not need a chat model.

options.text: A private connection from the agent to the search service does not automatically protect the search service's own connections to data sources and models
options.why: Correct. Inbound and outbound boundaries are separate.

questions.explanation: The retrieve API serves any client, and network isolation must be planned for each dependency.
